text:
sara: FYI seeing P95 token latency jump from ~180ms -> 1.2s for tenant `acme-ux` on dedicated pool eu-west-4 after the autoscale event at 09:02. Suspect GPU slice interference after we packed a new workload onto the node. attaching short logs.
mike: which pool/node? tenant id and recent deploy hash?
sara: pool dp-eu4-3, node gnode-47, tenant acme-ux, deploy v2.4.1. Logs: `2025-03-14T09:02:14Z request=tx123 p95=1.18s model=llama-70b` etc. No obvious error codes, just tails.
linus: ops-bot alert shows multiple MIG partitions on gnode-47 with mixed 1g/2g slices. after the autoscale we forced a pack which put a 2g tenant next to acme's 1g. SM util & memory bandwidth spikes line up.
ops-bot: [ALERT] High tail latency detected on dp-eu4-3 (p95 > 1s). Node: gnode-47. Active partitions: [1g,1g,2g,2g].
jess: I dumped `nvidia-smi pmon -c 1` and saw SM% oscillating 40->95 on slice 0 while slice 2 had frequent microbursts. Also saw periodic evictions from CUDA driver logs.
linus: can you paste the minimal repro? curious if it's steady-state or bursty.
sara: repro steps (short):
```
# hit acme inference route with 8 concurrent connections, 512 token prompts
for i in `seq 1 8`; do hey -n 500 -c 8 https://api.redwood.test/infer?tenant=acme-ux & done
```
observed p95 spike after ~90s, matches the autoscale churn window.
mike: looks like packing created heterogenous MIG neighbors causing L3/cache thrash. have we seen this before on 4g partitions?
jess: uncommon but possible if workloads have very different memory access patterns. can we get DCGM metrics (sm_util, sm_efficiency, l2_bandwidth) around the window? run:
```
dcgmmetrics --csv --metrics sm_launched,sm_efficiency,l2_read_throughput --duration 120 --interval 1 > /tmp/dcgm.csv
```
sara: attaching excerpt of dcgm: sm_efficiency on slice 0 dips to 12% during spike, l2_read_throughput spikes on slice 2. Also kernel dmesg shows `GPU eviction due to watchdog` twice.
linus: two immediate actions: 1) migrate acme-ux off gnode-47 to an isolated node, 2) enforce packing rules to avoid mixed sizes on that pool for now. long term: prefer same-size packing or soft isolation for high-p95 tenants.
mike: I'll open a rotation and bump autoscale min from 1->2 for the pool to avoid fractional packing when node churns. ETA ~45m to complete drain and move.
sara: TY. can you also flag this tenant for priority isolation? they have strict latency SLAs.
jess: quick mitigation command to move tenant (ops):
```
rbctl migrate-tenant --tenant acme-ux --target isolated-eu4-01 --force
```
mike: started migration job 1749998895, will monitor. added temporary placement rule `no-mix-1g-2g` to dp-eu4-3.
linus: please also collect `perf` counters on the node if migration doesn't bring p95 down. suspicious of L3 cache evictions and warps stalling.
sara: after migration p95 dropped to 190ms within 2 minutes, looks good. leaving this thread for postmortem notes.
jess: opened follow-up ticket INF-4782 to investigate packing heuristics and add a placement policy for latency-sensitive tenants. suggested changes: prefer equal-size packing, avoid bursty neighbors, add kernel-level perf sampling on pack events.
mike: will propose autoscale tweak in config PR today. good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
sara: closing loop here, will update customer and attach mitigation notes. :white_check_mark:
